Seminar Title:

Dynamics of Income Inequality in Developing Countries: The Role of Globalisation, Gender Inequality, and Environmental Degradation

Seminar Type:

Contact:

Jalandhar Pradhan

Abstract:

Income inequality refers to the unequal distribution of income among individuals, groups, populations, and social classes, where a large share of total income is concentrated in the hands of a few people. It denotes the disparity between high- and low-income earners, and it is frequently measured using tools such as the Gini coefficient. However, the Gini coefficient fails to capture the income concentration at the upper tail of the distribution. Therefore, this study took the Gini coefficient along with the top 1% and top 10% income shares. The unequal opportunities, structural inequality, and weak government redistribution lead to persistent income inequality in developing countries. Moreover, factors such as technological advancement, educational disparities, globalisation, and gender contribute to income inequality. With this background, the objective of the study are: first, to identify the determinants of income inequality and decompose the contribution of key drivers of income inequality in developing countries second, to examine whether economic, social, and political globalisations drives convergence or divergence in income inequality across developing countries third, to investigate the effect of gender inequality on income inequality in developing countries fourth, to analyse the spatial spillover effects of income inequality with environmental degradation in developing countries using spatial panel econometric models. This study will utilise data from various secondary sources, such as World Development Indicators (WDI), Standardised World Income Inequality Database (SWIID), World Inequality Database (WID), Penn World Table 10, KOF Swiss Economic Institute, International Monetary Fund (IMF), and United Nations Development Program (UNDP) from 2000 to 2023 for developing countries. An appropriate econometrics model will be used for the empirical analysis. The study findings will assist policymakers in designing targeted interventions to reduce income disparities, improve access to economic opportunities, and promote inclusive growth.

Keywords: Income inequality Gini coefficient Developing countries Spatial spillover effects Globalisation
